We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2{t}^{2}+t-2)+{x}_{2}({t}^{2}+3t-6)+{x}_{3}(-2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}) & =-2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+3t-6 \\ -2{x}_{3}{t}^{3}+(2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+({x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})t+(-2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}) & =-2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+3t-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=4 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -5{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-5{x}_{2}+3\cdot 1=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}+3\cdot 1=3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{2}=1.$
